name: CASH, the Hon. Michaelia Clare

headline.note: Freehills 1999–2008 employment now includes first-person evidence of a 12-month Melbourne secondment starting June 2001. Unsupported exact cessation proxy removed. Hours, leave, promotion and pre-1999 employment remain unknown; no full-time total calculated.

career_spells.role: Solicitor and senior associate, employment and industrial relations
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography and multiple professional/party biographies record legal practice at Freehills from 1999 to entry into Parliament in 2008, ultimately as a senior associate in employment and industrial relations. The exact 1999 start, promotion date, hours, leave, election campaign arrangements and final day are not published; 1 July 2008 is the Senate term start, not proved as the employment cessation date. Removed 1 July Senate-term commencement as unproved employer cessation proxy. First-person interview identifies Melbourne secondment beginning June 2001 for 12 months; nested detail below, not an additional employment interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is well supported, but substantive full-time status, exact boundaries and leave are insufficient for a documented full-time-years calculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: Biographies record Young Liberal, state-council, divisional and state-executive activity before Senate election. No paid party employment is established. Senate term start is not party-role cessation; unsupported exact endpoint removed. Individual party office dates remain to be mapped.
career_spells.counting_note: Party and candidate activity is excluded.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography records election in 2007 with the Senate term beginning 1 July 2008 and subsequent re-elections.

Cash directly reports June 2001 commencement and a 12-month secondment. Approximate return around June 2002 may be inferred, but no exact cessation or actual return date is supplied, so end remains null. Nested within 1999–2008 Freehills service; do not double-count. Full-time status and leave unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, substantive full-time status and/or leave remain insufficiently evidenced; no headline years calculated.

research_notes: Identify any paid employment between Cash's 1990 Curtin graduation and 1999 Freehills commencement, distinguishing overseas travel and legal study from employment.
Obtain Freehills appointment, admission and promotion dates, hours, leave and exact cessation, including the 2007 election campaign and interval before the Senate term began on 1 July 2008.
Confirm whether any Liberal Party position was paid employment rather than party governance or candidacy.

Follow-up 2026-10-02: reread full Thomson Reuters interview and identified previously unrecorded June 2001 Melbourne secondment, reported as 12 months. Dates and overlap are explicit; status remains unknown.

Searched first-job, overseas-work, admission, promotion and full-time-history terms; results did not establish additional paid employers, law admission/promotion dates or hours. Travel reporting alone is not paid employment evidence.

Next leads: historical Freehills staff biographies and annual reviews for 1999 appointment, secondment return and 2008 departure; public CV for 1990–1999 employment/study/travel overlap. Do not repeat generic biography searches without a new lead.

Follow-up 2026-10-03: targeted admission, legal-practice, preselection/campaign-leave, early-career and historical Senate-interest searches produced no defensible employment boundary beyond 1999–2008. A 24 June 1994 WA Government Gazette names Cash as a Commissioner for Declarations, but that appointment is not evidence of paid employment and was not converted into a career spell. Search-result admission fragments concerned other lawyers; they were rejected. Next useful evidence remains a historical Freehills staff record, practising-certificate/admission record tied to Cash, or a public CV documenting 1990–1999.
